stem:
Neil puts $\mathrm{Rs}\,4000$ in a simple-interest account at $8\%$ per year for $2$ years.

Which two claims are correct?

options.text: Year-$2$ interest is $8\%$ of the amount after year $1$, so the principal has grown.
Each year the interest is $8\%$ of the same principal $\mathrm{Rs}\,4000$.
Over $2$ years the interest totals $\mathrm{Rs}\,640$, because $2\times 0.08\times 4000=640$.
Simple interest at $8\%$ also covers every loan and deposit Neil will ever open.

teacher.key_rationale: Simple interest keeps the principal fixed, so each year uses 8% of Rs 4000 and two years give Rs 640. Treating year 2 as interest on a grown amount swaps in compounding. Claiming the same rule for every future account over-extends the scope.
